text:
You visit the local D-MOD service center to seek out a representative.

D-MOD welcomes any spacers who offer their ships as target practice in weapon demonstrations. These demonstrations serve as both entertainment to the local populace and a practical option for retiring captains wishing to cement their own decisions. 

Barring that, the more technical and savvy D-MOD employees seek out ships to creatively "modify", a desire largely satisfied by superstitious - yet wealthy - space captains who believe that a broken-down ship performs better than a pristine one.

After a short wait, a D-MOD representative establishes a comm-link with you to discuss their services and answer any queries you might have.

text:
You ask the D-MOD representative about using a ship from your fleet as target practice for the center's next weapons demonstration. The representative gleefully accepts your interest, sending you a TriPad regarding the center's Terms of Service.

Although a D-MOD demonstration will effectively cripple whatever ship you offer, the D-MOD representative reassures you that the ship will be recovered and returned to your fleet - albeit with some permanent damage. In exchange, the service center will provide some recompense in the form of credits, depending on the ship's initial hull integrity upon submission.

text: The D-MOD representative tells you that the $dmodservices_pickedShipName cannot be used as target practice, as the ship is far too damaged to remain recoverable after a demonstration.
You have offered a ship to the D-MOD representative. Some time later, you and your crew are invited to the demonstration area, where the $dmodservices_pickedShipName sits inert.

Soon after, a battery of weapon emplacements pound the helpless ship, forming a cloud of metal and sparks that obscure the view. The crowd roars with frenzied excitement as explosions continuously rock the spectator area.

Once the shaking ceases and the smoke finally clears, what was once an intact hull is now but a skeleton of its former self.

Soon after, a battery of Hephaestus Assault Guns pound the hapless ship. This epic barrage produces a deafening rhythm - a lasting heartbeat felt by everyone in the spectator area. Surrounding your viewing position, Hegemony officers and crew alike all stomp their boots in sync, roaring with the awesome might of the Hegemony Navy. You can feel the burning warmth of their comaraderie, almost as if you yourself were sustaining heavy ballistic gunfire from an Onslaught-class battleship.

Once the shelling barrage ends, the ship remains nothing more than molten slag, its skeletal hull a reminder of its former glory.

Suddenly, a flash of light zaps the unfortunate ship, then more flashes follow. Soon, a spectacle of directed beams puncture the hull, choreographed by automated entertainment systems designed to produce maximum audience excitement. Tri-Tachyon executives, unbothered by the blinding display, relax in the comfort of their luxurious hover-chairs, while a Company employee poses for a self-picture - presumably in a vain attempt to impress their TriLink peers.

Suddenly, a Tachyon Lance stream slices the perforated ship into measured pieces, marking the end of the demonstration as loud applause fills the spectator area.

A shield bubble envelops the defenseless ship. Then, an onslaught of machine gun fire splatters upon the shield bubble, emitting countless waves across the shield's arcs. Behind you is a Kazeronian navarch, lecturing their officers about the importance of combined arms tactics in fleet combat. As if to prove their point, a pair of red lasers touches the battered and weakened shield, followed by a massive blast of Dragonfire plasma that disintegrates the bubble and incinerates the ship underneath.

The navarch concludes their speech by emphasizing the League's collective mission to free the Persean Sector from hegemonic tyranny - symbolized by the blazing remains of your ship.

Before you can even get comfortable, however, a massive explosion vibrates the spectator area. A Hammer-class torpedo had dealt a lethal blow to the exposed ship, spraying debris wildly across the arena expanse. The crowd - mainly wealthy Luddic merchants, mixed with a few exhausted laborers and curious unbelievers - watches with wonder and glee. You catch a nearby Knight contemplating in prayer, murmuring something about the impermanence of life interweaving with the neverending duty to abide by Ludd's teachings.

As the ship slowly crumbles into jagged pieces - the consequence of a surgical torpedo strike - the crowd slowly disperses from the sorrowful display, returning once more to their daily habits.

A propaganda holovid plays out over the spectator area, voicing "the glory of Sindrian blood and the inviolable spirit of Andrada's will". Your eyes catch several Diktat officers and their subordinates in attendance. They align themselves in an unbroken formation, passively absorbing the spoken words. Suddenly, a purple glow envelops the entire demonstration area. A Gigacannon, pointed straight down at its prey, charges with an imposing, dreadful glare - a thundercloud, biding its time so it may strike down the unworthy. Then, the tense atmosphere breaks, the antimatter lightning obliterating the ship into dust right as the holovid and, in turn, the mesmerized audience hail Andrada.

Besides you and your fellow crew, no attention is paid to the now-lifeless husk that was once a ship.

The song and dance remains the same as the previous time: you watch as your offered ship is blasted apart, with onlookers expressing a wide range of emotions. At the end, all that remains is a pile of scrap metal and circuits barely maintaining its original shape.

text:
You ask about the D-MOD's specialized barratry services, knowing full well that they charge a hefty sum for such services. The D-MOD representative sends a request form to your TriPad, providing more details regarding this service.

The form includes the full procedure steps. First, a team of ship engineers will enter your ship to study its internals. Then, with the help of their own schematics and other proprietary machinations, these engineers will break your ship with such surgical precision that it will only gain the damage you wanted - and nothing more.

Of course, such talented labor requires commensurate payment, especially when the ship has already been damaged beyond permanent repair.

text:
You ask the D-MOD representative if they offer any options for removing special ship modifications - referring to the non-standard ship upgrades and not the so-called "special modifications" normally offered by D-MOD. The representative then hands you a TriPad containing the Terms and Conditions for this exclusive service, available only to "those who prove themselves as a valuable partner".

D-MOD is well-known by many for the corporation's "deconstructive" methods - a reputation further bolstered by its willingness to disassemble unwanted ship modifications for captains feeling the "modder's remorse". Given permission, an elite team of ship mechanics and engineers will, with utmost precision and care, identify and remove the targeted modifications from one of your ships - all without it suffering any permanent damage.

Naturally, like any worthwhile endeavor, this service will cost a pretty millicredit, or so the D-MOD representative says. You consider your options as you pore through the representative's TriPad.

id: # D-MOD option 4: Automate (requires discovery of a certain defender fleet)

text:
You ask if D-MOD's specialized technicians and engineers can automate one of your human-crewed ships. The D-MOD representative seems perplexed by your suggestion; you can hear faint whispers about the legality of this exotic request - no doubt wondering if this will incite another AI War.

After a short while - and to your surprise - the D-MOD representative requests that you provide them any data to assist the service center in creating automated ships. Apparently, this particular D-MOD center considers the profit made from satisfying your request worth the off-chance that a zealous Hegemony AI inspector might pay a visit the center for "suspicious activity".

As your fleet technicians transmit the relevant data for automating human-crewed ships, the D-MOD representative warns you that such a specialized service comes with huge expenses (though you suspect much of this expense is for paying off any potential AI inspections against the D-MOD center). Also, due to D-MOD's lack of documentation and experience, the automation process will not only inflict permanent damage on the ship, but this invasive and highly-complex process will also completely prevent any future ship restoration, making any ship damage incurred during and after the process permanent.
